text:
sam_ae: Hey team — EpsilonBank POC next Thurs 9am-3pm PST. They want to run heavy chat load and validate tail latency. Can we get an ephemeral pre-warm / headroom reservation on a dedicated pool? thinking ~8 GPUs for 6 hours plus a short burst window.
jamie_se: +1. Need to confirm autoscale policy and whether we can do soft-reserve (credit escrow) vs hard commit. Also need API keys and KMS scope for logs.
ryan_infra: We can spin an ephemeral pool tagged `eps-poc-prewarm`. Two modes: soft-headroom (credits escrow, usage capped) or short-term reservation (billing commit). Which does sales prefer?
sam_ae: Soft-headroom preferred to avoid commit, but they need predictable latency for demo. Can we guarantee no cold starts for a 1h pre-warm?
vikram_runtime: Yes — we can pre-load KV caches and keep workers warm. Need model + max seq len + expected concurrency to size prewarm tasks and KV warmers. Also we need the routing tag `route=eps-poc` so traffic hits the pool.
jamie_se: Model: `redwood-13b-v2-q4`. Seq len ~1024. Target peak concurrency: 120 qps (short bursts to 180).
ryan_infra: For soft-headroom plan: allocate pool with min=8 GPUs, max=16 GPUs, attach burst-credit bucket, and run prewarm job 60m before start. Will require credit escrow approval (PO or AE sign).
elain_csm: EpsilonBank asks for SSO and IP allowlist. They said for the demo hosted dedicated with IP allowlist is OK; private VPC not needed for this POC. KMS: restrict key access to pool service account and disable export.
sam_ae: I can approve escrow up to $2k for the session. Is that likely to be enough?
ryan_infra: Estimate: 8 GPUs for 6h + burst = ~$1.6k under our table, so $2k should be fine. If escrow depletes, we need a fallback policy — auto-throttle or model downgrade. Approve now?
sam_ae: Approve auto-fallback to `redwood-7b-v2-q4` plus throttling after escrow used. Document fallback in runbook.
vikram_runtime: Autoscale policy suggestion (json blob as config snippet):
```
{"min_gpus":"8","max_gpus":"16","scale_up_threshold_qps":"100","cooldown_seconds":"120","burst_credit_bucket":"eps-demo-credits","prewarm":"true","graceful_drain_seconds":"300"}
```
This will keep min warm and allow short spikes via credits.
jamie_se: Nice. Ops — can you create a scoped demo API key (read-only metrics + route tag) for AE and short-lived demo keys for the customer?
ryan_infra: Yes. Will create `eps-demo-read` key for AE (12h) and an `eps-demo-cust` key scoped to route+ip ACL for customer (valid 8h). Will store in vault and share via AE secure channel.
deploy-bot: pool `eps-poc-prewarm` provisioning scheduled by infra at 2025-11-06T15:00:00Z; will post status updates here. :white_check_mark:
jamie_se: Also need CIDR list for IP allowlist. Sam pls DM.
sam_ae: Sending CIDRs in DM: 54.12.34.0/24, 3.45.67.128/26.
elaine_csm: I'll attach the KMS checklist to the security questionnaire and flag the key policy restriction.
vikram_runtime: We'll add route-based fallback and a canary model pin. Prewarm job runs synthetic traffic generator 60m before and a smoke test 2h before demo with sanitized prompts. We'll post console traces.
jamie_se: One more pricing Q: if escrow exhausted mid-demo and fallback kicks in, will customer be billed for overage or will system throttle?
ryan_infra: For soft-headroom we cap to escrow; when depleted we will throttle or switch to fallback model. We will not auto-bill beyond escrow without explicit approval.
sam_ae: Good. Please ensure runbook includes escalation path if they want to convert to hard-reserve mid-demo.
vikram_runtime: Will do. Adding runbook note: contact infra oncall + AE to approve conversion; conversion time ~5-10m.
jamie_se: Great. Thanks team — I'll update EpsilonBank with approved plan (soft-headroom with prewarm, $2k escrow, fallback to 7b, IP allowlist). :thumbsup:
